name: Zuph
overview: Zuph was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted primarily as the father of Tohu and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel. His role is briefly mentioned in Scripture, emphasizing his place within the Levitical lineage. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zuph appears in Scripture without a given meaning. Another form of his name, Zophai, means "[dripping, full] honeycomb," which may reflect a characteristic or family name variant found in the genealogical records.
familyAndRelationships: Zuph is identified as the father of Tohu and the grandfather of Elkanah, making him an ancestor of Samuel. These relationships establish his place within a significant Levitical family line, though Scripture does not provide further familial details beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zuph's significance lies in his genealogical position as an ancestor of Samuel, one of Israel's greatest prophets. Through his lineage, the biblical narrative traces the heritage and priestly background that shaped Samuel's ministry. His mention underscores the importance of Levitical ancestry in the unfolding story of God's work in Israel.
